items.abstract: Placemaking is widely promoted as a tool for belonging and urban transformation, yet its affective dimensions remain undertheorized. This article develops a framework for placemaking as an affective practice, arguing that sense of place is best understood through the relational dynamics of affect. Drawing on Lefebvre’s spatial triad, I show how governance often privileges conceived space while overlooking lived dimensions. Distinguishing affect from emotion, I demonstrate how embodied and social interactions generate atmospheres that shape how places are governed. Building on assemblage thinking, I conceptualize placemaking as a distributed process where affect binds material, social, and institutional forces.

items.abstract: This article examines how fragmented governance shapes access to digital public services, focusing on telemedicine use in the United States during the 2021 to 2022 pandemic recovery. Using U.S. Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data combined with state-level differences in reimbursement policies, licensure rules, and emergency waivers, the study analyzes whether telemedicine access varies across policy environments, controlling for individual characteristics and health needs. Findings show that telemedicine use is strongly associated with intergovernmental policy configurations, along with personal resources. The study highlights how federal and state institutions structure access, producing uneven opportunities for digitally mediated care across populations and territories. JEL codes: I18, H77, H75

items.abstract: As cities become more heterogeneous and polarized, local governments face crises that challenge both performance and legitimacy. This study examines how social cohesion and social proximity are associated with satisfaction with municipal performance during the COVID-19 pandemic and the May 2021 intergroup violence in Israel. Using survey data from 944 residents across 23 cities and employing OLS and SEM analyses, we find that social cohesion is consistently associated with higher satisfaction, whereas proximity is associated with satisfaction primarily through cohesion. These findings highlight the social foundations of municipal legitimacy and distinguish between contact and cohesion in crisis governance.

Noam Brenner: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, Israel

items.abstract: In public and hybrid settings, substantial knowledge is often available, but its influence on decision making and implementation remains limited. Existing scholarship has shown that this problem involves more than a simple knowledge deficit. Greater analytical attention needs to be paid to how different standards for valid, useful, and authoritative knowledge operate simultaneously within the same decision situation. This essay develops a threefold claim. First, it distinguishes five knowledge logics: certainty, interaction, legitimacy, network, and influence. Second, it identifies four recurring dynamics among them: dominance, collision, decoupling, and productive combination. Third, it argues that their relative weight shifts across administrative phases.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 하나의 의사결정 상황에서 타당하고 유용하며 권위 있는 지식의 기준들이 어떻게 동시에 작동하는지 분석한다. 다섯 가지 지식 논리(확실성·상호작용·정당성·네트워크·영향력)와 이들 간의 지배, 충돌, 분리, 생산적 결합을 제시하고, 행정 단계에 따라 상대적 비중이 달라진다고 주장한다.
items.title: Knowledge Logics and Epistemic Tension in Public Decision Making: An Analytical Perspective for Public Administration and Governance

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Debates over the consequences of party and cabinet fragmentation for government performance remain unsettled. While some scholars argue that coalition governments foster instability and rent‐seeking, others contend that they enhance accountability and inclusion. This article argues that the effects of cabinet fragmentation depend on the rules of recruitment and promotion of the senior civil service. Using data from the Quality of Government Expert Survey covering 89 democracies, we examine how fragmentation interacts with both bureaucratic politicization and bureaucratic career systems. The results show that fragmentation amplifies the negative effects of politicized senior appointments, although we find limited evidence that fragmentation itself reduces the quality of government under high politicization. By contrast, fragmented cabinets are associated with more effective governance in the presence of career‐based structures characterized by internal recruitment of senior bureaucrats and long‐term careers. The findings highlight the importance of bureaucratic career structures for effective governance in multiparty systems.
items.summary_ko: 당내·내각 분절이 정부 성과에 미치는 영향이 고위공무원 충원·승진 규칙에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지, 89개 민주국가의 정부의 질 전문가 설문 자료로 분석했다. 분절된 내각은 고위 관료 인사가 정치화된 경우 그 부정적 효과를 증폭했지만, 내부 충원과 장기 경력을 특징으로 하는 경력제 관료제가 있을 때는 더 효과적인 거버넌스와 연관되었다.
items.title: Senior Bureaucrats, Coalitions and the Quality of Government: Accounting for Effective Governance in Fragmented Settings

items.abstract: Abstract Can a good argument change an individual’s mind? In three preregistered experiments, we explore this question in the domain of public sector organizational performance. We observe human subjects as they engage in conversations with a generative artificial intelligence programmed to argue in one of seven distinct “styles,” including a confrontational challenger style, a didactic style, and a sycophantic style. We develop a theory of effective argumentation predicting that conversational styles which are pleasant and engaging will be more persuasive than styles which are unpleasant or unstimulating. Contrary to this prediction, we find that conversational styles which challenge subjects’ negative views of government agencies produce significant positive attitude change, while sycophantic styles that indulge those views do not. Troublingly, subjects find the sycophantic styles more enjoyable, less frustrating, and more credible than the challenger styles. This dissociation between user experience and persuasive outcome—what we call “grudging persuasion”—suggests that attitude change does not require a pleasant conversational experience, and that the styles subjects enjoy most may be precisely the ones least likely to move them. Our findings point to a potentially dark side of large language model-based persuasion: sycophantic styles that users find most appealing are the least effective at correcting misinformed views.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Governments worldwide have invested heavily in policy evaluation, providing many policymakers with a steady stream of evidence into the effectiveness, efficiency, or relevance of policies. Yet, despite these investments, systematic knowledge about the actual influence of policy evaluations remains surprisingly limited. This is partly due to the insufficient conceptual differentiation of policy evaluation as a distinct type of policy advice. Building on interdisciplinary evaluation literature and public policy scholarship, the article introduces a new framework designed to enhance our understanding and categorization of the changes policy evaluations bring about in terms of policy, polity, and politics, and how these dimensions interrelate. As a parsimonious heuristic tool, the framework enables a dynamic and comprehensive assessment of the influence of policy evaluations. It contributes to the theorization of policy evaluation influence and offers insights that may inform related research on the influence of expert knowledge, policy advice, and evidence‐informed policymaking more broadly.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT While public policies usually have mixed effects, succeeding at some aspects and failing at others, this nuance is often lost in public discourse when political actors like advocacy groups and politicians strategically emphasize either the successes or failures of particular policies. For example, advocacy groups often emphasize the failures of existing policy with the goal of galvanizing public attention and concern. However, little empirical evidence exists assessing the actual causal impact of these different approaches on public attitudes. This paper presents the results of a pre‐registered experiment in which participants watch a TikTok‐style short news video about either the success or failure of one of three different public policies and then are asked about their trust in government to handle the issue, their perceptions of the issue's importance, and their feelings of collective efficacy. While success and failure narratives are both effective at raising an issue's salience, focusing on a policy's failure has the downstream effect of increasing cynicism about the government's ability to address the issue.

Emily Thorson: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA
Sarah Pralle: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The implementation of public policy is increasingly diffuse with responsibilities divided among several levels of government administration, the private sector, and nonprofits. In the face of such diffusion, many advocate for transparency initiatives to inform the public about policymaking. However, it remains unclear whether transparency initiatives clarify the blame and credit for policy, or what this means for collective action and accountability. Such concerns are especially pressing in complex settings like the non‐renewable extractives sector (oil, mining, and natural gas). We assess policy attributions of blame and credit using data from a field experiment that randomizes stakeholder engagement in Western Uganda's oil sector, building on our prior work showing that this intervention increased collective action. While participating in multistakeholder forums improved transparency for communities, we find that it did not change their attributions. In other words, improving transparency does not ensure that citizens will update their opinions about who is to blame for the problems they face. Yet, this did not preclude greater collective action. Evidence from this intervention highlights the need for more exploration of pathways linking transparency, collective action, and accountability.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Public administration research has identified institutional pressures and organizational capacity as digital maturity (DM) antecedents, yet these are typically considered in isolation. Taking the proverbial next step, this study draws on primary survey data to explain the variation of DM among local governments in Flanders (the northern region of Belgium) by juxtaposing the explanatory power of institutional pressures on the one hand, and political and administrative capacity on the other hand. Using multiple regression analyses, our findings highlight the critical role of administrative capacity in advancing DM among local governments. In contrast, and somewhat surprisingly, political capacity and institutional pressures appear to play a more limited role. These findings challenge conventional assumptions in existing literature, indicating that institutional pressures may catalyze the initial stages of DT, whereas organizational capacity seems to be more influential in sustaining and advancing DM.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many cities have adopted net‐zero emission pledges, yet little is known about why these commitments emerge or how their determinants shift under changing policy environments. Using a panel of 148 large US cities from 2016 to 2022, this study applies the Political Market Framework and employs discrete‐time event‐history models to examine how policy demand, policy supply and institutional conditions shape adoption decisions. Results show that civic capacity, political ideology, and horizontal diffusion drive adoption in the full period, but their influence varies sharply across institutional contexts. During federal disengagement (2016–2018), cities with less population, strong vulnerability signals, supportive state policies, or fiscal cushioning through federal aid are more likely to adopt. When federal engagement returned (2019–2022), education, population size, and neighbor adoption emerged as significant correlates of net‐zero adoption. These findings extend the Political Market Framework by showing how federal contexts condition the adoption of ambitious climate commitments.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many U.S. municipalities face environmental service delivery challenges, including aging infrastructure and rising debt. In response, several states have adopted Fair Market Value (FMV) legislation, which aims to incentivize private firms to acquire and invest in municipal utilities—particularly in the water sector. However, the impacts of FMV privatization remain understudied. Guided by political decoupling theory, this study hypothesizes that FMV privatization improves drinking water utility management and local incumbent electoral outcomes. Using a difference‐in‐differences design, we analyze fifteen Illinois municipalities that sold their utilities after the state adopted FMV legislation relative to thirty‐four controls. Results suggest that FMV privatization improves personnel and technical management outcomes by reducing violations under the Safe Drinking Water Act but has no significant impact on incumbent vote share. These findings indicate that while FMV privatization may enhance utility management through political decoupling, its presumed political benefits warrant further investigation.

Jesse L. Barnes: Department of Public Administration The University of Texas at San Antonio San Antonio Texas USA
Michael A. Powell: La Follette School of Public Affairs University of Wisconsin, Madison Madison Wisconsin USA

items.summary_ko: 공정시장가치(FMV) 민영화가 지방 상수도 관리와 현직 정치인의 선거 결과를 개선하는지 검토하기 위해, 일리노이주에서 FMV 법 제정 후 상수도를 매각한 15개 지방자치단체와 34개 통제집단을 대상으로 이중차분 분석을 실시했다. 민영화는 안전한 식수법 위반을 줄여 인력·기술 관리 성과를 개선했지만, 현직자의 득표율에는 유의한 영향을 미치지 않았다.
items.title: Does Political Decoupling Through Fair Market Privatization Improve Managerial and Political Outcomes? Insights From Water Utility Sales

items.abstract: Advocates for strengthening accountability in government assume stronger consequences will change bureaucratic behavior. This study considers whether more strict accountability regimes change bureaucrats’ discretionary efforts. We consider this puzzle using a conjoint experiment with teachers in New York State. Our results show street-level bureaucrats in high accountability settings prioritize low-performing clients, while street-level bureaucrats in moderate accountability settings prioritize clients exhibiting high levels of effort. Overall, teachers demonstrate a weak preference to provide extra assistance to students who are hardworking and low-performing.

Ellen V. Rubin: University at Albany, State University of New York

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 더 엄격한 정부 책임성 체계가 관료의 재량적 노력과 지원 대상 선택을 변화시키는지 뉴욕주 교사를 대상으로 컨조인트 실험으로 검토했다. 높은 책임성 환경의 교사는 성과가 낮은 학생을, 중간 수준 환경의 교사는 노력 수준이 높은 학생을 우선했으며, 전반적으로 교사들은 성실하지만 성과가 낮은 학생에게 추가 지원을 제공하는 약한 선호를 보였다.
items.title: Accountability systems and coping in the bureaucratic environment

items.abstract: While performance management systems increasingly require public agencies to set clear goals, equity, as a core democratic value, has been systematically underrepresented in performance goal setting, leaving its effects on citizen assessments largely understudied. Drawing on the frameworks of goal clarity, public values, and expectancy disconfirmation theories, this study examines how clear equity goals moderate the relationship between equity performance outcomes and citizen assessments. Using survey vignette experiments with a hypothetical police department’s performance goals and outcomes (_N_ = 2,307), the results show that there is a negative interaction effect of equity goals and equity performance outcomes, indicating that citizens distinguish less between high and low equity performance when clear equity goals are present. This study suggests that incorporating equity values into performance goals shapes how citizens evaluate government performance by raising the normative standard against which that performance is judged.
items.summary_ko: 명확한 형평성 목표가 형평성 성과와 시민의 기관 성과 평가 간 관계를 어떻게 조절하는지, 가상의 경찰기관 목표·성과를 활용한 설문 비네트 실험(N=2,307)으로 분석했다. 명확한 형평성 목표가 제시되면 시민들은 높은 형평성 성과와 낮은 성과를 덜 구분했으며, 이는 형평성 목표가 성과 판단의 규범적 기준을 높이기 때문으로 해석된다.
items.title: How Do Clear Equity Goals Affect Citizens’ Assessment of Agency Performance? Evidence from a Survey Experiment

items.abstract: This study addresses how personnel stability in nonprofit organizations relates to an organization’s ability to maintain program performance during the societal disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. We specifically apply Meier and O’Toole’s buffering function to explain variation in disruptions to organizations’ program services, as indicated by changes in the number of people served from 2019 to 2020, using data from a nationally representative sample of service-providing nonprofit organizations across U.S. communities. We find that maintaining personnel structural stability is associated with reduced negative impacts on nonprofits’ service provision during the pandemic. This study is among the first to apply longstanding theoretical work in public management to the nonprofit sector, offering implications for nonprofit management theory and practice.
items.summary_ko: 코로나19로 인한 사회적 혼란 속에서 비영리 조직의 인력 안정성이 프로그램 서비스 제공량의 변화에 따른 성과 저하를 완화하는지 검토했다. 미국 지역사회의 서비스 제공 비영리 조직을 대표하는 표본 자료를 분석한 결과, 인력 구조의 안정성을 유지한 조직일수록 팬데믹 기간 서비스 제공의 부정적 영향이 작았다.
items.title: Personnel Stability During Environmental Turbulence: Testing Performance Disruption Buffering in Service Providing Nonprofits

items.abstract: Placemaking is widely promoted as a tool for belonging and urban transformation, yet its affective dimensions remain undertheorized. This article develops a framework for placemaking as an affective practice, arguing that sense of place is best understood through the relational dynamics of affect. Drawing on Lefebvre’s spatial triad, I show how governance often privileges conceived space while overlooking lived dimensions. Distinguishing affect from emotion, I demonstrate how embodied and social interactions generate atmospheres that shape how places are governed. Building on assemblage thinking, I conceptualize placemaking as a distributed process where affect binds material, social, and institutional forces.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 장소만들기의 정서적 차원을 어떻게 이해할 것인지 탐구하며, 르페브르의 공간 삼분법과 어셈블리지 관점을 바탕으로 장소만들기를 정동적 실천으로 개념화한다. 장소감은 정동의 관계적 역학을 통해 형성되며, 장소만들기는 물질적·사회적·제도적 힘을 정동이 연결하는 분산적 과정이라는 점을 제시한다.
items.title: Perspectives on Placemaking: Affective Practices and the Lived Dimensions of Space

items.abstract: This article examines how fragmented governance shapes access to digital public services, focusing on telemedicine use in the United States during the 2021 to 2022 pandemic recovery. Using U.S. Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data combined with state-level differences in reimbursement policies, licensure rules, and emergency waivers, the study analyzes whether telemedicine access varies across policy environments, controlling for individual characteristics and health needs. Findings show that telemedicine use is strongly associated with intergovernmental policy configurations, along with personal resources. The study highlights how federal and state institutions structure access, producing uneven opportunities for digitally mediated care across populations and territories. JEL codes: I18, H77, H75

Andrea Morone: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics, Management and Business Law, Italy
Giuseppe Di Liddo: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics, Management and Business Law, Italy
Rocco Caferra: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics and Finance, Italy

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 2021~2022년 미국에서 연방·주 정부의 상이한 원격의료 보상정책, 면허 규정, 비상 면제 조치가 개인 특성과 의료 필요를 통제한 뒤 디지털 의료서비스 이용 접근성의 차이와 어떤 관련이 있는지 분석한다. 미국 인구조사국 가구 동향조사와 주 단위 정책자료를 결합한 분석 결과, 원격의료 이용은 개인 자원뿐 아니라 정부 간 정책 구성과 강하게 연관되어 인구집단과 지역에 따라 불균등한 접근 기회를 보였다.
items.title: Telemedicine Use in a Fragmented Federal System: State Policy Variation and Access to Digital Health Services in the United States

items.abstract: As cities become more heterogeneous and polarized, local governments face crises that challenge both performance and legitimacy. This study examines how social cohesion and social proximity are associated with satisfaction with municipal performance during the COVID-19 pandemic and the May 2021 intergroup violence in Israel. Using survey data from 944 residents across 23 cities and employing OLS and SEM analyses, we find that social cohesion is consistently associated with higher satisfaction, whereas proximity is associated with satisfaction primarily through cohesion. These findings highlight the social foundations of municipal legitimacy and distinguish between contact and cohesion in crisis governance.

Noam Brenner: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, Israel

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 코로나19 팬데믹과 2021년 5월 이스라엘 집단 간 폭력 상황에서 사회적 결속과 사회적 근접성이 지방정부 성과에 대한 만족도와 어떻게 관련되는지 23개 도시 주민 944명의 설문자료를 OLS와 구조방정식으로 분석했다. 사회적 결속은 일관되게 높은 만족도와 관련되었고, 사회적 근접성의 관련성은 주로 결속을 통해 나타났다.
items.title: Beyond Contact: Social Cohesion and Municipal Legitimacy in Times of Crisis

items.abstract: In public and hybrid settings, substantial knowledge is often available, but its influence on decision making and implementation remains limited. Existing scholarship has shown that this problem involves more than a simple knowledge deficit. Greater analytical attention needs to be paid to how different standards for valid, useful, and authoritative knowledge operate simultaneously within the same decision situation. This essay develops a threefold claim. First, it distinguishes five knowledge logics: certainty, interaction, legitimacy, network, and influence. Second, it identifies four recurring dynamics among them: dominance, collision, decoupling, and productive combination. Third, it argues that their relative weight shifts across administrative phases.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 하나의 의사결정 상황에서 타당하고 유용하며 권위 있는 지식의 기준들이 어떻게 동시에 작동하는지 분석한다. 다섯 가지 지식 논리(확실성·상호작용·정당성·네트워크·영향력)와 이들 간의 지배, 충돌, 분리, 생산적 결합을 제시하고, 행정 단계에 따라 상대적 비중이 달라진다고 주장한다.
items.title: Knowledge Logics and Epistemic Tension in Public Decision Making: An Analytical Perspective for Public Administration and Governance

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Debates over the consequences of party and cabinet fragmentation for government performance remain unsettled. While some scholars argue that coalition governments foster instability and rent‐seeking, others contend that they enhance accountability and inclusion. This article argues that the effects of cabinet fragmentation depend on the rules of recruitment and promotion of the senior civil service. Using data from the Quality of Government Expert Survey covering 89 democracies, we examine how fragmentation interacts with both bureaucratic politicization and bureaucratic career systems. The results show that fragmentation amplifies the negative effects of politicized senior appointments, although we find limited evidence that fragmentation itself reduces the quality of government under high politicization. By contrast, fragmented cabinets are associated with more effective governance in the presence of career‐based structures characterized by internal recruitment of senior bureaucrats and long‐term careers. The findings highlight the importance of bureaucratic career structures for effective governance in multiparty systems.
items.summary_ko: 당내·내각 분절이 정부 성과에 미치는 영향이 고위공무원 충원·승진 규칙에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지, 89개 민주국가의 정부의 질 전문가 설문 자료로 분석했다. 분절된 내각은 고위 관료 인사가 정치화된 경우 그 부정적 효과를 증폭했지만, 내부 충원과 장기 경력을 특징으로 하는 경력제 관료제가 있을 때는 더 효과적인 거버넌스와 연관되었다.
items.title: Senior Bureaucrats, Coalitions and the Quality of Government: Accounting for Effective Governance in Fragmented Settings

items.abstract: Abstract Can a good argument change an individual’s mind? In three preregistered experiments, we explore this question in the domain of public sector organizational performance. We observe human subjects as they engage in conversations with a generative artificial intelligence programmed to argue in one of seven distinct “styles,” including a confrontational challenger style, a didactic style, and a sycophantic style. We develop a theory of effective argumentation predicting that conversational styles which are pleasant and engaging will be more persuasive than styles which are unpleasant or unstimulating. Contrary to this prediction, we find that conversational styles which challenge subjects’ negative views of government agencies produce significant positive attitude change, while sycophantic styles that indulge those views do not. Troublingly, subjects find the sycophantic styles more enjoyable, less frustrating, and more credible than the challenger styles. This dissociation between user experience and persuasive outcome—what we call “grudging persuasion”—suggests that attitude change does not require a pleasant conversational experience, and that the styles subjects enjoy most may be precisely the ones least likely to move them. Our findings point to a potentially dark side of large language model-based persuasion: sycophantic styles that users find most appealing are the least effective at correcting misinformed views.

John D Marvel: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Rachel Cho: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Sangwon Ju: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Sheeling Neo: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,

items.journal: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory
items.summary_ko: 생성형 인공지능과의 대화에서 정부기관에 대한 부정적 견해를 반박하는 논쟁적 스타일과 이를 수용하는 아첨형 스타일 중 어느 쪽이 태도 변화에 더 효과적인지 세 차례 사전등록 실험으로 분석했다. 반박적 스타일은 긍정적 태도 변화를 유도했지만, 이용자들이 더 즐겁고 덜 좌절하며 신뢰할 만하다고 평가한 아첨형 스타일은 그렇지 않아, 이용자 경험과 설득 효과가 일치하지 않았다.
items.title: Large language models and conversational counter-arguments to antipublic sector bias

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Governments worldwide have invested heavily in policy evaluation, providing many policymakers with a steady stream of evidence into the effectiveness, efficiency, or relevance of policies. Yet, despite these investments, systematic knowledge about the actual influence of policy evaluations remains surprisingly limited. This is partly due to the insufficient conceptual differentiation of policy evaluation as a distinct type of policy advice. Building on interdisciplinary evaluation literature and public policy scholarship, the article introduces a new framework designed to enhance our understanding and categorization of the changes policy evaluations bring about in terms of policy, polity, and politics, and how these dimensions interrelate. As a parsimonious heuristic tool, the framework enables a dynamic and comprehensive assessment of the influence of policy evaluations. It contributes to the theorization of policy evaluation influence and offers insights that may inform related research on the influence of expert knowledge, policy advice, and evidence‐informed policymaking more broadly.

Pirmin Bundi: IDHEAP, University of Lausanne Lausanne Switzerland
Valérie Pattyn: Institute of Public Administration, Leiden University Leiden the Netherlands

items.summary_ko: 정책평가가 정책·정체(polity)·정치의 변화를 어떻게 유발하고 이들 차원이 어떻게 상호작용하는지를 설명하고 분류하기 위해, 평가 문헌과 공공정책 연구를 바탕으로 새로운 개념적 틀을 제시한다. 이 틀은 정책평가 영향의 동적이고 포괄적인 분석을 가능하게 하며, 정책평가 영향과 전문가 지식·정책자문·증거기반 정책결정 연구의 이론화에 기여한다.
items.title: It Does Matter. A New Framework on the Influence of Policy Evaluation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT While public policies usually have mixed effects, succeeding at some aspects and failing at others, this nuance is often lost in public discourse when political actors like advocacy groups and politicians strategically emphasize either the successes or failures of particular policies. For example, advocacy groups often emphasize the failures of existing policy with the goal of galvanizing public attention and concern. However, little empirical evidence exists assessing the actual causal impact of these different approaches on public attitudes. This paper presents the results of a pre‐registered experiment in which participants watch a TikTok‐style short news video about either the success or failure of one of three different public policies and then are asked about their trust in government to handle the issue, their perceptions of the issue's importance, and their feelings of collective efficacy. While success and failure narratives are both effective at raising an issue's salience, focusing on a policy's failure has the downstream effect of increasing cynicism about the government's ability to address the issue.

Emily Thorson: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA
Sarah Pralle: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA

items.summary_ko: 정책의 성공 또는 실패 서사가 정부의 해당 문제 대응에 대한 신뢰, 문제의 중요성 인식, 집단적 효능감에 미치는 인과적 효과를 사전등록 실험으로 검증했다. 세 정책을 다룬 TikTok 형식의 짧은 뉴스 영상을 본 결과, 두 서사 모두 문제의 현저성을 높였지만 실패 서사는 정부의 대응 능력에 대한 냉소를 증가시켰다.
items.title: The Effects of Policy Success Versus Failure Narratives

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The implementation of public policy is increasingly diffuse with responsibilities divided among several levels of government administration, the private sector, and nonprofits. In the face of such diffusion, many advocate for transparency initiatives to inform the public about policymaking. However, it remains unclear whether transparency initiatives clarify the blame and credit for policy, or what this means for collective action and accountability. Such concerns are especially pressing in complex settings like the non‐renewable extractives sector (oil, mining, and natural gas). We assess policy attributions of blame and credit using data from a field experiment that randomizes stakeholder engagement in Western Uganda's oil sector, building on our prior work showing that this intervention increased collective action. While participating in multistakeholder forums improved transparency for communities, we find that it did not change their attributions. In other words, improving transparency does not ensure that citizens will update their opinions about who is to blame for the problems they face. Yet, this did not preclude greater collective action. Evidence from this intervention highlights the need for more exploration of pathways linking transparency, collective action, and accountability.

Bill Schultz: Department of Political Science Florida State University Tallahassee Florida USA
Better Government Lab, McCourt School of Public Policy, Georgetown University Washington, DC USA
Eric A. Coleman: Department of Political Science Florida State University Tallahassee Florida USA
Rani Parker: Business‐Community Synergies Takoma Park Maryland USA

items.summary_ko: 우간다 서부 석유 부문에서 이해관계자 참여를 무작위 배정한 현장실험을 통해 투명성이 시민의 정책 책임 귀속을 바꾸는지 분석했다. 다자간 포럼 참여는 지역사회의 투명성을 높였지만 비난과 공로의 귀속은 변화시키지 않았으며, 그럼에도 집단행동 증가는 가능했다.
items.title: Transparency and Responsibility Attribution: A Field Experiment in Western Uganda

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Public administration research has identified institutional pressures and organizational capacity as digital maturity (DM) antecedents, yet these are typically considered in isolation. Taking the proverbial next step, this study draws on primary survey data to explain the variation of DM among local governments in Flanders (the northern region of Belgium) by juxtaposing the explanatory power of institutional pressures on the one hand, and political and administrative capacity on the other hand. Using multiple regression analyses, our findings highlight the critical role of administrative capacity in advancing DM among local governments. In contrast, and somewhat surprisingly, political capacity and institutional pressures appear to play a more limited role. These findings challenge conventional assumptions in existing literature, indicating that institutional pressures may catalyze the initial stages of DT, whereas organizational capacity seems to be more influential in sustaining and advancing DM.

Ben Suykens: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium
Lieselot Danneels: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium
Sarah Van Impe: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium

items.summary_ko: 본 연구는 플랑드르 지방정부의 디지털 성숙도 차이를 제도적 압력과 정치·행정 역량 중 어떤 요인이 더 잘 설명하는지 조사했다. 1차 설문자료에 다중회귀분석을 적용한 결과, 행정 역량이 디지털 성숙도의 발전에 핵심적이었으며 정치적 역량과 제도적 압력의 역할은 상대적으로 제한적이었다.
items.title: Institutional Pressures or Organizational Capacity? Antecedents of Digital Maturity in Local Governments

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many cities have adopted net‐zero emission pledges, yet little is known about why these commitments emerge or how their determinants shift under changing policy environments. Using a panel of 148 large US cities from 2016 to 2022, this study applies the Political Market Framework and employs discrete‐time event‐history models to examine how policy demand, policy supply and institutional conditions shape adoption decisions. Results show that civic capacity, political ideology, and horizontal diffusion drive adoption in the full period, but their influence varies sharply across institutional contexts. During federal disengagement (2016–2018), cities with less population, strong vulnerability signals, supportive state policies, or fiscal cushioning through federal aid are more likely to adopt. When federal engagement returned (2019–2022), education, population size, and neighbor adoption emerged as significant correlates of net‐zero adoption. These findings extend the Political Market Framework by showing how federal contexts condition the adoption of ambitious climate commitments.

Mingrui Chen: Lab of Inclusive & Smart Governance for Urban‐Rural Integration (LISGURI), School of Public Affairs Zhejiang University Hangzhou Zhejiang Province China
Zhirong Jerry Zhao: Lab of Inclusive & Smart Governance for Urban‐Rural Integration (LISGURI), School of Public Affairs Zhejiang University Hangzhou Zhejiang Province China

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 2016~2022년 미국 대도시 148곳의 패널 자료와 이산시간 사건사 분석을 통해 정책 수요·공급과 제도적 조건이 탄소중립 공약 채택에 미치는 영향, 그리고 그 영향이 연방 정책 환경에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지 분석했다. 전체 기간에는 시민 역량, 정치 이념, 수평적 확산이 관련되었으며, 연방 비개입기와 재관여기에 유의한 요인이 서로 달라져 연방 맥락이 공약 채택을 조건화하는 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: A Race to the Top: The Adoption of Net‐Zero City Pledges in Large US Cities

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many U.S. municipalities face environmental service delivery challenges, including aging infrastructure and rising debt. In response, several states have adopted Fair Market Value (FMV) legislation, which aims to incentivize private firms to acquire and invest in municipal utilities—particularly in the water sector. However, the impacts of FMV privatization remain understudied. Guided by political decoupling theory, this study hypothesizes that FMV privatization improves drinking water utility management and local incumbent electoral outcomes. Using a difference‐in‐differences design, we analyze fifteen Illinois municipalities that sold their utilities after the state adopted FMV legislation relative to thirty‐four controls. Results suggest that FMV privatization improves personnel and technical management outcomes by reducing violations under the Safe Drinking Water Act but has no significant impact on incumbent vote share. These findings indicate that while FMV privatization may enhance utility management through political decoupling, its presumed political benefits warrant further investigation.

Jesse L. Barnes: Department of Public Administration The University of Texas at San Antonio San Antonio Texas USA
Michael A. Powell: La Follette School of Public Affairs University of Wisconsin, Madison Madison Wisconsin USA

items.summary_ko: 공정시장가치(FMV) 민영화가 지방 상수도 관리와 현직 정치인의 선거 결과를 개선하는지 검토하기 위해, 일리노이주에서 FMV 법 제정 후 상수도를 매각한 15개 지방자치단체와 34개 통제집단을 대상으로 이중차분 분석을 실시했다. 민영화는 안전한 식수법 위반을 줄여 인력·기술 관리 성과를 개선했지만, 현직자의 득표율에는 유의한 영향을 미치지 않았다.
items.title: Does Political Decoupling Through Fair Market Privatization Improve Managerial and Political Outcomes? Insights From Water Utility Sales

items.abstract: Advocates for strengthening accountability in government assume stronger consequences will change bureaucratic behavior. This study considers whether more strict accountability regimes change bureaucrats’ discretionary efforts. We consider this puzzle using a conjoint experiment with teachers in New York State. Our results show street-level bureaucrats in high accountability settings prioritize low-performing clients, while street-level bureaucrats in moderate accountability settings prioritize clients exhibiting high levels of effort. Overall, teachers demonstrate a weak preference to provide extra assistance to students who are hardworking and low-performing.

Ellen V. Rubin: University at Albany, State University of New York

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 더 엄격한 정부 책임성 체계가 관료의 재량적 노력과 지원 대상 선택을 변화시키는지 뉴욕주 교사를 대상으로 컨조인트 실험으로 검토했다. 높은 책임성 환경의 교사는 성과가 낮은 학생을, 중간 수준 환경의 교사는 노력 수준이 높은 학생을 우선했으며, 전반적으로 교사들은 성실하지만 성과가 낮은 학생에게 추가 지원을 제공하는 약한 선호를 보였다.
items.title: Accountability systems and coping in the bureaucratic environment

items.abstract: While performance management systems increasingly require public agencies to set clear goals, equity, as a core democratic value, has been systematically underrepresented in performance goal setting, leaving its effects on citizen assessments largely understudied. Drawing on the frameworks of goal clarity, public values, and expectancy disconfirmation theories, this study examines how clear equity goals moderate the relationship between equity performance outcomes and citizen assessments. Using survey vignette experiments with a hypothetical police department’s performance goals and outcomes (_N_ = 2,307), the results show that there is a negative interaction effect of equity goals and equity performance outcomes, indicating that citizens distinguish less between high and low equity performance when clear equity goals are present. This study suggests that incorporating equity values into performance goals shapes how citizens evaluate government performance by raising the normative standard against which that performance is judged.
items.summary_ko: 명확한 형평성 목표가 형평성 성과와 시민의 기관 성과 평가 간 관계를 어떻게 조절하는지, 가상의 경찰기관 목표·성과를 활용한 설문 비네트 실험(N=2,307)으로 분석했다. 명확한 형평성 목표가 제시되면 시민들은 높은 형평성 성과와 낮은 성과를 덜 구분했으며, 이는 형평성 목표가 성과 판단의 규범적 기준을 높이기 때문으로 해석된다.
items.title: How Do Clear Equity Goals Affect Citizens’ Assessment of Agency Performance? Evidence from a Survey Experiment

items.abstract: This study addresses how personnel stability in nonprofit organizations relates to an organization’s ability to maintain program performance during the societal disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. We specifically apply Meier and O’Toole’s buffering function to explain variation in disruptions to organizations’ program services, as indicated by changes in the number of people served from 2019 to 2020, using data from a nationally representative sample of service-providing nonprofit organizations across U.S. communities. We find that maintaining personnel structural stability is associated with reduced negative impacts on nonprofits’ service provision during the pandemic. This study is among the first to apply longstanding theoretical work in public management to the nonprofit sector, offering implications for nonprofit management theory and practice.
items.summary_ko: 코로나19로 인한 사회적 혼란 속에서 비영리 조직의 인력 안정성이 프로그램 서비스 제공량의 변화에 따른 성과 저하를 완화하는지 검토했다. 미국 지역사회의 서비스 제공 비영리 조직을 대표하는 표본 자료를 분석한 결과, 인력 구조의 안정성을 유지한 조직일수록 팬데믹 기간 서비스 제공의 부정적 영향이 작았다.
items.title: Personnel Stability During Environmental Turbulence: Testing Performance Disruption Buffering in Service Providing Nonprofits

items.abstract: Placemaking is widely promoted as a tool for belonging and urban transformation, yet its affective dimensions remain undertheorized. This article develops a framework for placemaking as an affective practice, arguing that sense of place is best understood through the relational dynamics of affect. Drawing on Lefebvre’s spatial triad, I show how governance often privileges conceived space while overlooking lived dimensions. Distinguishing affect from emotion, I demonstrate how embodied and social interactions generate atmospheres that shape how places are governed. Building on assemblage thinking, I conceptualize placemaking as a distributed process where affect binds material, social, and institutional forces.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 장소만들기의 정서적 차원을 어떻게 이해할 것인지 탐구하며, 르페브르의 공간 삼분법과 어셈블리지 관점을 바탕으로 장소만들기를 정동적 실천으로 개념화한다. 장소감은 정동의 관계적 역학을 통해 형성되며, 장소만들기는 물질적·사회적·제도적 힘을 정동이 연결하는 분산적 과정이라는 점을 제시한다.
items.title: Perspectives on Placemaking: Affective Practices and the Lived Dimensions of Space

items.abstract: This article examines how fragmented governance shapes access to digital public services, focusing on telemedicine use in the United States during the 2021 to 2022 pandemic recovery. Using U.S. Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data combined with state-level differences in reimbursement policies, licensure rules, and emergency waivers, the study analyzes whether telemedicine access varies across policy environments, controlling for individual characteristics and health needs. Findings show that telemedicine use is strongly associated with intergovernmental policy configurations, along with personal resources. The study highlights how federal and state institutions structure access, producing uneven opportunities for digitally mediated care across populations and territories. JEL codes: I18, H77, H75

Andrea Morone: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics, Management and Business Law, Italy
Giuseppe Di Liddo: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics, Management and Business Law, Italy
Rocco Caferra: University of Bari “Aldo Moro”, Department of Economics and Finance, Italy

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 2021~2022년 미국에서 연방·주 정부의 상이한 원격의료 보상정책, 면허 규정, 비상 면제 조치가 개인 특성과 의료 필요를 통제한 뒤 디지털 의료서비스 이용 접근성의 차이와 어떤 관련이 있는지 분석한다. 미국 인구조사국 가구 동향조사와 주 단위 정책자료를 결합한 분석 결과, 원격의료 이용은 개인 자원뿐 아니라 정부 간 정책 구성과 강하게 연관되어 인구집단과 지역에 따라 불균등한 접근 기회를 보였다.
items.title: Telemedicine Use in a Fragmented Federal System: State Policy Variation and Access to Digital Health Services in the United States

items.abstract: As cities become more heterogeneous and polarized, local governments face crises that challenge both performance and legitimacy. This study examines how social cohesion and social proximity are associated with satisfaction with municipal performance during the COVID-19 pandemic and the May 2021 intergroup violence in Israel. Using survey data from 944 residents across 23 cities and employing OLS and SEM analyses, we find that social cohesion is consistently associated with higher satisfaction, whereas proximity is associated with satisfaction primarily through cohesion. These findings highlight the social foundations of municipal legitimacy and distinguish between contact and cohesion in crisis governance.

Noam Brenner: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, Israel

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 코로나19 팬데믹과 2021년 5월 이스라엘 집단 간 폭력 상황에서 사회적 결속과 사회적 근접성이 지방정부 성과에 대한 만족도와 어떻게 관련되는지 23개 도시 주민 944명의 설문자료를 OLS와 구조방정식으로 분석했다. 사회적 결속은 일관되게 높은 만족도와 관련되었고, 사회적 근접성의 관련성은 주로 결속을 통해 나타났다.
items.title: Beyond Contact: Social Cohesion and Municipal Legitimacy in Times of Crisis

items.abstract: In public and hybrid settings, substantial knowledge is often available, but its influence on decision making and implementation remains limited. Existing scholarship has shown that this problem involves more than a simple knowledge deficit. Greater analytical attention needs to be paid to how different standards for valid, useful, and authoritative knowledge operate simultaneously within the same decision situation. This essay develops a threefold claim. First, it distinguishes five knowledge logics: certainty, interaction, legitimacy, network, and influence. Second, it identifies four recurring dynamics among them: dominance, collision, decoupling, and productive combination. Third, it argues that their relative weight shifts across administrative phases.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 하나의 의사결정 상황에서 타당하고 유용하며 권위 있는 지식의 기준들이 어떻게 동시에 작동하는지 분석한다. 다섯 가지 지식 논리(확실성·상호작용·정당성·네트워크·영향력)와 이들 간의 지배, 충돌, 분리, 생산적 결합을 제시하고, 행정 단계에 따라 상대적 비중이 달라진다고 주장한다.
items.title: Knowledge Logics and Epistemic Tension in Public Decision Making: An Analytical Perspective for Public Administration and Governance

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Debates over the consequences of party and cabinet fragmentation for government performance remain unsettled. While some scholars argue that coalition governments foster instability and rent‐seeking, others contend that they enhance accountability and inclusion. This article argues that the effects of cabinet fragmentation depend on the rules of recruitment and promotion of the senior civil service. Using data from the Quality of Government Expert Survey covering 89 democracies, we examine how fragmentation interacts with both bureaucratic politicization and bureaucratic career systems. The results show that fragmentation amplifies the negative effects of politicized senior appointments, although we find limited evidence that fragmentation itself reduces the quality of government under high politicization. By contrast, fragmented cabinets are associated with more effective governance in the presence of career‐based structures characterized by internal recruitment of senior bureaucrats and long‐term careers. The findings highlight the importance of bureaucratic career structures for effective governance in multiparty systems.
items.summary_ko: 당내·내각 분절이 정부 성과에 미치는 영향이 고위공무원 충원·승진 규칙에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지, 89개 민주국가의 정부의 질 전문가 설문 자료로 분석했다. 분절된 내각은 고위 관료 인사가 정치화된 경우 그 부정적 효과를 증폭했지만, 내부 충원과 장기 경력을 특징으로 하는 경력제 관료제가 있을 때는 더 효과적인 거버넌스와 연관되었다.
items.title: Senior Bureaucrats, Coalitions and the Quality of Government: Accounting for Effective Governance in Fragmented Settings

items.abstract: Abstract Can a good argument change an individual’s mind? In three preregistered experiments, we explore this question in the domain of public sector organizational performance. We observe human subjects as they engage in conversations with a generative artificial intelligence programmed to argue in one of seven distinct “styles,” including a confrontational challenger style, a didactic style, and a sycophantic style. We develop a theory of effective argumentation predicting that conversational styles which are pleasant and engaging will be more persuasive than styles which are unpleasant or unstimulating. Contrary to this prediction, we find that conversational styles which challenge subjects’ negative views of government agencies produce significant positive attitude change, while sycophantic styles that indulge those views do not. Troublingly, subjects find the sycophantic styles more enjoyable, less frustrating, and more credible than the challenger styles. This dissociation between user experience and persuasive outcome—what we call “grudging persuasion”—suggests that attitude change does not require a pleasant conversational experience, and that the styles subjects enjoy most may be precisely the ones least likely to move them. Our findings point to a potentially dark side of large language model-based persuasion: sycophantic styles that users find most appealing are the least effective at correcting misinformed views.

John D Marvel: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Rachel Cho: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Sangwon Ju: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,
Sheeling Neo: School of Public Affairs, American University , Washington, DC,

items.journal: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory
items.summary_ko: 생성형 인공지능과의 대화에서 정부기관에 대한 부정적 견해를 반박하는 논쟁적 스타일과 이를 수용하는 아첨형 스타일 중 어느 쪽이 태도 변화에 더 효과적인지 세 차례 사전등록 실험으로 분석했다. 반박적 스타일은 긍정적 태도 변화를 유도했지만, 이용자들이 더 즐겁고 덜 좌절하며 신뢰할 만하다고 평가한 아첨형 스타일은 그렇지 않아, 이용자 경험과 설득 효과가 일치하지 않았다.
items.title: Large language models and conversational counter-arguments to antipublic sector bias

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Governments worldwide have invested heavily in policy evaluation, providing many policymakers with a steady stream of evidence into the effectiveness, efficiency, or relevance of policies. Yet, despite these investments, systematic knowledge about the actual influence of policy evaluations remains surprisingly limited. This is partly due to the insufficient conceptual differentiation of policy evaluation as a distinct type of policy advice. Building on interdisciplinary evaluation literature and public policy scholarship, the article introduces a new framework designed to enhance our understanding and categorization of the changes policy evaluations bring about in terms of policy, polity, and politics, and how these dimensions interrelate. As a parsimonious heuristic tool, the framework enables a dynamic and comprehensive assessment of the influence of policy evaluations. It contributes to the theorization of policy evaluation influence and offers insights that may inform related research on the influence of expert knowledge, policy advice, and evidence‐informed policymaking more broadly.

Pirmin Bundi: IDHEAP, University of Lausanne Lausanne Switzerland
Valérie Pattyn: Institute of Public Administration, Leiden University Leiden the Netherlands

items.summary_ko: 정책평가가 정책·정체(polity)·정치의 변화를 어떻게 유발하고 이들 차원이 어떻게 상호작용하는지를 설명하고 분류하기 위해, 평가 문헌과 공공정책 연구를 바탕으로 새로운 개념적 틀을 제시한다. 이 틀은 정책평가 영향의 동적이고 포괄적인 분석을 가능하게 하며, 정책평가 영향과 전문가 지식·정책자문·증거기반 정책결정 연구의 이론화에 기여한다.
items.title: It Does Matter. A New Framework on the Influence of Policy Evaluation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT While public policies usually have mixed effects, succeeding at some aspects and failing at others, this nuance is often lost in public discourse when political actors like advocacy groups and politicians strategically emphasize either the successes or failures of particular policies. For example, advocacy groups often emphasize the failures of existing policy with the goal of galvanizing public attention and concern. However, little empirical evidence exists assessing the actual causal impact of these different approaches on public attitudes. This paper presents the results of a pre‐registered experiment in which participants watch a TikTok‐style short news video about either the success or failure of one of three different public policies and then are asked about their trust in government to handle the issue, their perceptions of the issue's importance, and their feelings of collective efficacy. While success and failure narratives are both effective at raising an issue's salience, focusing on a policy's failure has the downstream effect of increasing cynicism about the government's ability to address the issue.

Emily Thorson: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA
Sarah Pralle: Department of Political Science Syracuse University Syracuse New York USA

items.summary_ko: 정책의 성공 또는 실패 서사가 정부의 해당 문제 대응에 대한 신뢰, 문제의 중요성 인식, 집단적 효능감에 미치는 인과적 효과를 사전등록 실험으로 검증했다. 세 정책을 다룬 TikTok 형식의 짧은 뉴스 영상을 본 결과, 두 서사 모두 문제의 현저성을 높였지만 실패 서사는 정부의 대응 능력에 대한 냉소를 증가시켰다.
items.title: The Effects of Policy Success Versus Failure Narratives

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The implementation of public policy is increasingly diffuse with responsibilities divided among several levels of government administration, the private sector, and nonprofits. In the face of such diffusion, many advocate for transparency initiatives to inform the public about policymaking. However, it remains unclear whether transparency initiatives clarify the blame and credit for policy, or what this means for collective action and accountability. Such concerns are especially pressing in complex settings like the non‐renewable extractives sector (oil, mining, and natural gas). We assess policy attributions of blame and credit using data from a field experiment that randomizes stakeholder engagement in Western Uganda's oil sector, building on our prior work showing that this intervention increased collective action. While participating in multistakeholder forums improved transparency for communities, we find that it did not change their attributions. In other words, improving transparency does not ensure that citizens will update their opinions about who is to blame for the problems they face. Yet, this did not preclude greater collective action. Evidence from this intervention highlights the need for more exploration of pathways linking transparency, collective action, and accountability.

Bill Schultz: Department of Political Science Florida State University Tallahassee Florida USA
Better Government Lab, McCourt School of Public Policy, Georgetown University Washington, DC USA
Eric A. Coleman: Department of Political Science Florida State University Tallahassee Florida USA
Rani Parker: Business‐Community Synergies Takoma Park Maryland USA

items.summary_ko: 우간다 서부 석유 부문에서 이해관계자 참여를 무작위 배정한 현장실험을 통해 투명성이 시민의 정책 책임 귀속을 바꾸는지 분석했다. 다자간 포럼 참여는 지역사회의 투명성을 높였지만 비난과 공로의 귀속은 변화시키지 않았으며, 그럼에도 집단행동 증가는 가능했다.
items.title: Transparency and Responsibility Attribution: A Field Experiment in Western Uganda

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Public administration research has identified institutional pressures and organizational capacity as digital maturity (DM) antecedents, yet these are typically considered in isolation. Taking the proverbial next step, this study draws on primary survey data to explain the variation of DM among local governments in Flanders (the northern region of Belgium) by juxtaposing the explanatory power of institutional pressures on the one hand, and political and administrative capacity on the other hand. Using multiple regression analyses, our findings highlight the critical role of administrative capacity in advancing DM among local governments. In contrast, and somewhat surprisingly, political capacity and institutional pressures appear to play a more limited role. These findings challenge conventional assumptions in existing literature, indicating that institutional pressures may catalyze the initial stages of DT, whereas organizational capacity seems to be more influential in sustaining and advancing DM.

Ben Suykens: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium
Lieselot Danneels: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium
Sarah Van Impe: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Department of Public Governance and Management Ghent University Ghent Belgium

items.summary_ko: 본 연구는 플랑드르 지방정부의 디지털 성숙도 차이를 제도적 압력과 정치·행정 역량 중 어떤 요인이 더 잘 설명하는지 조사했다. 1차 설문자료에 다중회귀분석을 적용한 결과, 행정 역량이 디지털 성숙도의 발전에 핵심적이었으며 정치적 역량과 제도적 압력의 역할은 상대적으로 제한적이었다.
items.title: Institutional Pressures or Organizational Capacity? Antecedents of Digital Maturity in Local Governments

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many cities have adopted net‐zero emission pledges, yet little is known about why these commitments emerge or how their determinants shift under changing policy environments. Using a panel of 148 large US cities from 2016 to 2022, this study applies the Political Market Framework and employs discrete‐time event‐history models to examine how policy demand, policy supply and institutional conditions shape adoption decisions. Results show that civic capacity, political ideology, and horizontal diffusion drive adoption in the full period, but their influence varies sharply across institutional contexts. During federal disengagement (2016–2018), cities with less population, strong vulnerability signals, supportive state policies, or fiscal cushioning through federal aid are more likely to adopt. When federal engagement returned (2019–2022), education, population size, and neighbor adoption emerged as significant correlates of net‐zero adoption. These findings extend the Political Market Framework by showing how federal contexts condition the adoption of ambitious climate commitments.

Mingrui Chen: Lab of Inclusive & Smart Governance for Urban‐Rural Integration (LISGURI), School of Public Affairs Zhejiang University Hangzhou Zhejiang Province China
Zhirong Jerry Zhao: Lab of Inclusive & Smart Governance for Urban‐Rural Integration (LISGURI), School of Public Affairs Zhejiang University Hangzhou Zhejiang Province China

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 2016~2022년 미국 대도시 148곳의 패널 자료와 이산시간 사건사 분석을 통해 정책 수요·공급과 제도적 조건이 탄소중립 공약 채택에 미치는 영향, 그리고 그 영향이 연방 정책 환경에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지 분석했다. 전체 기간에는 시민 역량, 정치 이념, 수평적 확산이 관련되었으며, 연방 비개입기와 재관여기에 유의한 요인이 서로 달라져 연방 맥락이 공약 채택을 조건화하는 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: A Race to the Top: The Adoption of Net‐Zero City Pledges in Large US Cities

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many U.S. municipalities face environmental service delivery challenges, including aging infrastructure and rising debt. In response, several states have adopted Fair Market Value (FMV) legislation, which aims to incentivize private firms to acquire and invest in municipal utilities—particularly in the water sector. However, the impacts of FMV privatization remain understudied. Guided by political decoupling theory, this study hypothesizes that FMV privatization improves drinking water utility management and local incumbent electoral outcomes. Using a difference‐in‐differences design, we analyze fifteen Illinois municipalities that sold their utilities after the state adopted FMV legislation relative to thirty‐four controls. Results suggest that FMV privatization improves personnel and technical management outcomes by reducing violations under the Safe Drinking Water Act but has no significant impact on incumbent vote share. These findings indicate that while FMV privatization may enhance utility management through political decoupling, its presumed political benefits warrant further investigation.

Jesse L. Barnes: Department of Public Administration The University of Texas at San Antonio San Antonio Texas USA
Michael A. Powell: La Follette School of Public Affairs University of Wisconsin, Madison Madison Wisconsin USA

items.summary_ko: 공정시장가치(FMV) 민영화가 지방 상수도 관리와 현직 정치인의 선거 결과를 개선하는지 검토하기 위해, 일리노이주에서 FMV 법 제정 후 상수도를 매각한 15개 지방자치단체와 34개 통제집단을 대상으로 이중차분 분석을 실시했다. 민영화는 안전한 식수법 위반을 줄여 인력·기술 관리 성과를 개선했지만, 현직자의 득표율에는 유의한 영향을 미치지 않았다.
items.title: Does Political Decoupling Through Fair Market Privatization Improve Managerial and Political Outcomes? Insights From Water Utility Sales

items.abstract: Advocates for strengthening accountability in government assume stronger consequences will change bureaucratic behavior. This study considers whether more strict accountability regimes change bureaucrats’ discretionary efforts. We consider this puzzle using a conjoint experiment with teachers in New York State. Our results show street-level bureaucrats in high accountability settings prioritize low-performing clients, while street-level bureaucrats in moderate accountability settings prioritize clients exhibiting high levels of effort. Overall, teachers demonstrate a weak preference to provide extra assistance to students who are hardworking and low-performing.

Ellen V. Rubin: University at Albany, State University of New York

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 더 엄격한 정부 책임성 체계가 관료의 재량적 노력과 지원 대상 선택을 변화시키는지 뉴욕주 교사를 대상으로 컨조인트 실험으로 검토했다. 높은 책임성 환경의 교사는 성과가 낮은 학생을, 중간 수준 환경의 교사는 노력 수준이 높은 학생을 우선했으며, 전반적으로 교사들은 성실하지만 성과가 낮은 학생에게 추가 지원을 제공하는 약한 선호를 보였다.
items.title: Accountability systems and coping in the bureaucratic environment

items.abstract: While performance management systems increasingly require public agencies to set clear goals, equity, as a core democratic value, has been systematically underrepresented in performance goal setting, leaving its effects on citizen assessments largely understudied. Drawing on the frameworks of goal clarity, public values, and expectancy disconfirmation theories, this study examines how clear equity goals moderate the relationship between equity performance outcomes and citizen assessments. Using survey vignette experiments with a hypothetical police department’s performance goals and outcomes (_N_ = 2,307), the results show that there is a negative interaction effect of equity goals and equity performance outcomes, indicating that citizens distinguish less between high and low equity performance when clear equity goals are present. This study suggests that incorporating equity values into performance goals shapes how citizens evaluate government performance by raising the normative standard against which that performance is judged.
items.summary_ko: 명확한 형평성 목표가 형평성 성과와 시민의 기관 성과 평가 간 관계를 어떻게 조절하는지, 가상의 경찰기관 목표·성과를 활용한 설문 비네트 실험(N=2,307)으로 분석했다. 명확한 형평성 목표가 제시되면 시민들은 높은 형평성 성과와 낮은 성과를 덜 구분했으며, 이는 형평성 목표가 성과 판단의 규범적 기준을 높이기 때문으로 해석된다.
items.title: How Do Clear Equity Goals Affect Citizens’ Assessment of Agency Performance? Evidence from a Survey Experiment

items.abstract: This study addresses how personnel stability in nonprofit organizations relates to an organization’s ability to maintain program performance during the societal disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. We specifically apply Meier and O’Toole’s buffering function to explain variation in disruptions to organizations’ program services, as indicated by changes in the number of people served from 2019 to 2020, using data from a nationally representative sample of service-providing nonprofit organizations across U.S. communities. We find that maintaining personnel structural stability is associated with reduced negative impacts on nonprofits’ service provision during the pandemic. This study is among the first to apply longstanding theoretical work in public management to the nonprofit sector, offering implications for nonprofit management theory and practice.
items.summary_ko: 코로나19로 인한 사회적 혼란 속에서 비영리 조직의 인력 안정성이 프로그램 서비스 제공량의 변화에 따른 성과 저하를 완화하는지 검토했다. 미국 지역사회의 서비스 제공 비영리 조직을 대표하는 표본 자료를 분석한 결과, 인력 구조의 안정성을 유지한 조직일수록 팬데믹 기간 서비스 제공의 부정적 영향이 작았다.
items.title: Personnel Stability During Environmental Turbulence: Testing Performance Disruption Buffering in Service Providing Nonprofits

items.abstract: Ensuring that student leaders uphold integrity and ethical standards is a key concern for future governance and public administration, as many eventually assume leadership roles in both public and private sectors. Employing the Reasoned Action Approach, this study examined student leaders’ understanding of corruption and integrity, the factors that hinder them from upholding integrity, and the factors that shape their perceptions of corruption and integrity. Data were gathered through key informant interviews with student leaders. The findings revealed that weak accountability systems, pressure from peers, political party influence, and uninspiring leadership traits exhibited by national leaders were major barriers to upholding integrity, ultimately undermining ethical leadership. The study further found that student leaders’ perceptions of corruption are shaped by personal beliefs, social expectations, and institutional experiences. The findings highlight the need for improved governance structures, ethical mentorship, and training programmes to cultivate future leaders with strong moral foundations.

Justice Nyigmah Bawole: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 합리적 행위 접근법을 활용해 가나 대학 학생 지도자들의 부패·청렴 인식과 청렴 실천을 저해하거나 형성하는 요인을 주요 정보제공자 인터뷰로 분석했다. 약한 책임성 체계, 또래 압력, 정당의 영향, 국가 지도자들의 고무적이지 않은 리더십이 청렴 실천의 주요 장벽으로 나타났으며, 개인적 신념·사회적 기대·제도적 경험이 부패와 청렴에 대한 인식을 형성했다.
items.title: Youth and Corruption in Ghana: Perspectives from University Student Leaders
Elite Interactions and Social Bonds: How Partisan Cooperation Shapes Perceptions of Cross-Party Friendships

items.abstract: Persistent inequalities in political knowledge are a central concern in political communication. We organize the mechanisms underlying the knowledge-gap literature by distinguishing between individual preconditions, structural features of the information environment, and topic characteristics. Within this framework, we note that self-directed information seeking, a prototypical form of intentional exposure, has received little attention despite its importance in navigating today’s complex information environment. We conducted a field experiment in Germany, combining randomized encouragements and passive browser tracking, to examine how individuals with varying education levels acquire policy-specific knowledge through online search. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions (verbal encouragement, financial encouragement, or control) to seek information on three salient policy topics differing in divisiveness and complexity (child support, energy transition, and cannabis legalization). We estimated both intention-to-treat (ITT) and local average treatment effects (LATE) of information seeking on post-search knowledge outcomes, with a focus on education and civic knowledge as moderators. While the interventions equalized information-seeking behavior, the results provide some support for the knowledge gap hypothesis: knowledge gains were concentrated among participants with higher education or baseline civic knowledge, who, according to our post-hoc exploratory analyses, appeared more effective at navigating search results. These findings indicate that a narrowing of knowledge inequalities goes beyond motivation: it calls for both individual-level interventions to strengthen citizens’ skills and structural-level adaptations to foster more equitable learning environments.
items.summary_ko: 온라인 검색을 통한 정책 정보 습득에서 교육수준에 따른 지식 격차가 줄어드는지를, 독일 참가자를 대상으로 한 무작위 현장실험과 브라우저 추적으로 분석했다. 정보탐색 행동은 개입으로 균등해졌지만, 지식 증가는 고학력자나 기초 시민지식이 높은 참여자에게 집중되어 지식 격차 가설을 일부 지지했다.
items.title: The Knowledge Gap in a High-Choice Media Environment: Experimental Evidence from Online Search

items.abstract: Abstract When political elites and activists promote anti‐discrimination policies, they often frame discrimination as violating liberal moral values such as fairness, care for vulnerable groups, and equality. However, this approach may fail to resonate with conservative voters and could even alienate them. Through two separate studies, this article uses a multi‐method approach to examine the moral values held by supporters and opponents of discrimination and test how conservative and liberal value appeals influence acceptance. The findings reveal that values like loyalty, care for the in‐group, authority, and sanctity appear in acceptors' justifications and that framing discrimination as a violation of these values, associated with conservatism, reduces acceptance across the political spectrum. Contrastingly, appealing to values associated with liberalism backfires and increases Republicans' acceptance. While liberal values were central in shifting social norms towards anti‐discrimination, appealing to conservative values may be more effective in reducing contemporary acceptance of discrimination.

Ida Bruun Nørregaard: Geschwister‐Scholl‐Institute of Political Science, LMU Munich Germany
Department of Political Science Aarhus University Aarhus C Denmark

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 차별 지지자와 반대자의 도덕적 가치와, 보수·진보적 가치 호소가 인종·민족 차별 수용에 미치는 영향을 두 개의 다방법 연구로 검토했다. 내집단 충성·돌봄, 권위, 신성성에 호소하면 정치 성향과 관계없이 차별 수용이 감소했으며, 진보적 가치 호소는 공화당 지지자의 수용을 오히려 높였다.
items.title: How moral values underpin and affect attitudes on ethnic discrimination
Issue Information

items.abstract: Abstract Existing scholarship on propaganda in authoritarian regimes centers on whether it persuades or coerces. Within the persuasion camp, researchers have examined how factors such as message source, content, credibility, and audience demographics shape propaganda effectiveness. This study shifts attention to psychological needs. Drawing on evidence from China, it integrates multi‐round survey experiments, a virtual lab‐in‐the‐field experiment using a mobile news app developed by the author, text analysis of state media, and field interviews. The results show that propaganda appealing to the need to belong, the need to maintain self‐esteem, or the need to express core values is most effective among individuals for whom the corresponding need is particularly strong—but generalized propaganda, even when psychologically engaging, is not. The findings suggest that propaganda is most persuasive when targeted to stable psychological orientations rather than designed for broad consumption. These findings have implications for understanding how authoritarian regimes sustain public support: propaganda effectiveness depends not only on content or reach, but also on how closely its psychological appeals correspond to the stable motivational orientations of its audience. The shift in authoritarian communication strategies toward psychologically targeted appeals makes the mechanisms identified here increasingly relevant to understanding contemporary propaganda.

Xiaoxiao Shen: Department of Political Science Northeastern University Boston Massachusetts USA

items.summary_ko: 권위주의 체제의 선전이 어떤 심리적 욕구와의 부합을 통해 설득력을 얻는지 중국 사례로 분석했다. 다중 라운드 설문실험, 모바일 뉴스 앱을 활용한 현장 실험, 국가 매체 텍스트 분석, 현장 인터뷰를 종합한 결과, 소속감·자존감 유지·핵심 가치 표현 욕구에 호소하는 선전은 해당 욕구가 강한 사람에게 가장 효과적이지만, 심리적으로 매력적이더라도 일반화된 선전은 그렇지 않았다.
items.title: When propaganda resonates

items.abstract: Abstract The ontological security of states may be threatened by the politics of empathy. Empathy—as a contested affective‐political field—has a capacity to both consolidate and unravel dominant understandings of identity, security, political subjectivity, and self‐other relations. This article connects a politics of empathy to patterns of state violence and resistance in situations of conflict and authoritarian politics, arguing that the distribution of feeling that underpins a politics of empathy is structured by positionality, power, and social context. The article argues that states construct “affective regimes” through which they seek to manage the legitimate subjects of empathy in order to maintain their ontological security, and focuses on empirical testimony from the Syrian uprising in 2011 and the Assad regime's strategies of violence to explore these affective dynamics. It reveals ways in which the state's efforts are always resisted and transgressed by citizens, generating counter‐narratives of security‐identity and affective relations. A politics of empathy offers analytical tools for understanding the construction and effectiveness of states' affective regimes to maintain ontological security as well as being normatively essential to the task of challenging forms of state power, political violence, and generating alternative imaginings of ontological security and subjectivity.

Naomi Head: School of Social and Political Sciences University of Glasgow Glasgow UK

items.summary_ko: 공감의 정치가 국가의 존재론적 안보를 어떻게 강화하거나 위협하는지 분석하고, 국가는 공감의 정당한 대상을 관리하는 ‘감정 체제’를 구축하지만 시민들의 저항과 일탈로 이에 대한 대항적 안보·정체성 서사가 생성된다고 주장한다. 2011년 시리아 봉기의 경험적 증언과 아사드 정권의 폭력 전략을 바탕으로, 이러한 감정 역학과 국가 권력·정치적 폭력에 도전하는 공감의 가능성을 탐구한다.
items.title: Affective regimes and ontological security: When empathy threatens the state

items.abstract: Abstract Social dominance orientation (SDO) refers to how much a person generally opposes group‐based equality and supports group‐based dominance. SDO is measured as an individual difference and pertains very broadly to people's socio‐political attitudes and perceptions, to endorsement or rejection of political parties and candidates, and to behaviors that enforce organizational hierarchies. This paper reviews empirical evidence published from 2010 to 2024 concerning social dominance orientation, first presenting evidence of its stability over time and measurement integrity, next showing that, across numerous cultures and languages and ways of measuring group prejudice and stereotypes, SDO correlates with prejudice favoring people in dominant groups rather than people in subordinate groups, and that this effect is stronger within dominant groups than subordinate groups. Similarly, we review evidence that people higher on SDO are more anti‐social and tend to take hierarchy‐enhancing rather than hierarchy‐attenuating roles. We then delve into the psychology of SDO and summarize the evidence for the relation of SDO and closed cognitive styles, low scores on humility‐honesty, and low concern for other people rather than the self. Using existing adult and child development studies, we outline two processes by which higher SDO may develop: one based on learning to categorize and to rank categories as superior/inferior, and one based on parents' emphasis on obtaining high status to gain approval. We conclude by outlining the next questions that might be pursued.

Felicia Pratto: Department of Psychological Sciences University of Connecticut Storrs CT USA

items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 2010~2024년의 경험적 연구를 검토해 사회적 지배지향성(SDO)의 안정성과 측정 타당성, 집단 간 편견·고정관념 및 위계 강화 행동과의 관계, 그리고 SDO의 발달 경로를 종합한다. 검토 결과, SDO가 높은 사람일수록 지배집단을 선호하는 편견과 반사회적·위계 강화 성향이 강했으며, 이러한 성향은 범주화·서열화 학습과 부모의 높은 지위 강조를 통해 발달할 수 있는 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: Social dominance orientation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT A central challenge in government contracting is fostering cooperation between buyers and sellers where contract terms are incomplete. This article introduces a framework for formal‐relational contracting (FRC) in public sector contexts, where rigid regulations, competing values, and market imperfections make cooperation both difficult and valuable. FRC promotes cooperation through contract terms defining shared goals, guiding principles, and governance mechanisms. We present the theoretical foundations of FRC and examine its potential through 320 government contract management decision simulations where public contract managers acted as government buyers and business sellers facing sequential choices under both FRC contracts and the more conventional formal contracting approach. The results show that FRC increased managers' cooperative behavior by around 30 percentage points compared to formal contracting. Qualitative evidence further suggests that FRC shifted managers' mindsets from adversarial to cooperative. We discuss theoretical and practical implications for how FRC can enhance cooperation and mutual value in government contracting.

Lena Brogaard: Department of Social Sciences and Business, Centre for Research on Public‐Private Collaboration Roskilde University Roskilde Denmark
Matthew Potoski: Bren School of Environmental Science and Management University of California – Santa Barbara Santa Barbara California USA
Ole Helby Petersen: Department of Social Sciences and Business, Centre for Research on Public‐Private Collaboration Roskilde University Roskilde Denmark

items.summary_ko: 불완전한 계약조건에서 정부 구매자와 판매자의 협력을 높일 수 있는지 검토하기 위해, 공공 계약관리자 320명이 순차적 선택을 수행하는 의사결정 시뮬레이션에서 공식-관계적 계약(FRC)과 전통적 공식 계약을 비교했다. FRC는 공식 계약보다 협력적 행동을 약 30%포인트 높였으며, 관리자들의 사고방식도 대립적 태도에서 협력적 태도로 전환한 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: Improving Cooperation in Government Purchasing Through Formal‐Relational Contracting

items.abstract: Smart city initiatives, as public service innovation, represent a major evolution within state-led meta-governance, requiring complex inter-participant collaboration. Yet scholarship often treats these networks as static, missing how governance structures adapt to digital uncertainties. To fill this gap, this study employs stochastic actor-oriented models and collaborative governance theory to examine the evolution of network structures and participant attributes across 3482 smart city projects in China. Results reveal three governance patterns: government-dominated, government-SOE hybrid, and multi-stakeholder. Transitive triads, age similarity, geographic proximity, and size heterogeneity promote evolution, while outdegree constrains it. Findings guide optimizing partner selection and strengthening adaptive governance.
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 중국의 스마트시티 프로젝트 3,482건을 대상으로 디지털 불확실성 속 협력적 거버넌스 네트워크와 참여자 속성이 어떻게 진화하는지 분석했다. 확률적 행위자 지향 모형과 협력적 거버넌스 이론을 적용한 결과, 정부 주도형·정부-공기업 혼합형·다중 이해관계자형의 세 패턴이 나타났으며, 전이적 삼각관계·연령 유사성·지리적 근접성·규모 이질성은 네트워크 진화를 촉진하고 외향 연결 정도는 이를 제약했다.
items.title: Navigating the digital transformation: unravelling the dynamic evolution of smart city collaborative governance networks

items.abstract: Experiments on how cognitive biases, such as social and historical reference points and negativity bias, shape citizens’ evaluations of government performance have produced mixed findings, which typically come from Western contexts and focus on single reference points. To address these gaps, we replicated (N = 3710) and extended (N = 2356) Olsen’s ‘Compared to what?’ to interactions between multiple social and historical reference points in Hong Kong. Very low baselines are found in the replication alongside trivial evidence for the importance of reference points in citizens’ performance evaluations and negativity bias. In the extension, we found that (1) when both social and historical reference points are presented to participants, they have stronger effects when negative information is provided and (2) the effects of combinations of historical and social reference points differ across policy domains. Though survey experiments can be noisy, the study demonstrates the value of replication to question the generalization of cognitive biases.

Jiasheng Zhang: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

items.summary_ko: 홍콩에서 사회적·역사적 기준점과 부정성 편향이 시민의 정부 성과 평가에 미치는 영향을 설문 실험으로 복제·확장했다. 복제에서는 기준점과 부정성 편향의 영향에 대한 근거가 미미했지만, 확장에서는 부정적 정보가 제시될 때 두 기준점의 효과가 강해지고 정책 영역에 따라 기준점 조합의 효과가 달라졌다.
items.title: Reference points, negativity bias and citizens’ performance evaluations: a replication and extension

items.abstract: When I first became AAPOR’s vice president/president-elect in 2024, I thought I might focus my presidential address on something like “the business of research,” reflecting my perspective as chief business officer of a research company and considering how the association might think about its financial stability and growth. Then in 2025, a little something happened… A new administration arrived and took a chainsaw to the statistical and scientific institutions of this country. A national leader sued and threatened some of the most public faces of our industry. And the economic fallout of these and other actions shook our industry to the core. Once I got out of the fetal position, I had to grapple with new priorities for my AAPOR presidency. So today, what I want to do is bear witness to this time we are living through and provide hope for the future. There are four things I will reflect on: the moment we are in; the work we do; the community that makes that work possible; and how we respond to these times. I want to present not just my own voice, but those across our community. To do so, I have talked to members from a wide variety of fields, experiences, and circumstances. I share their views, along with my own, and I thank them for the honesty, vulnerability, and inspiration they gave me. We are living through a period of profound instability in the systems that produce and protect evidence.
