Fernando D. Domingos: Sao Paulo School of Business Administration, Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV EAESP) São Paulo São Paulo Brazil
Michael Gibson: Government Outcomes Lab (GOLab), Blavatnik School of Government, University of Oxford Oxford UK
Vinícius M. Magnani: School of Economics, Business and Accounting of Ribeirão Preto (FEA‐RP), Universidade de São Paulo (USP) Ribeirão Preto São Paulo Brazil

items.summary_ko: 성과기반 공공서비스 계약에서 투자자 지향성(사회적·재무적·이중 목적)이 투자 약정 규모와 어떻게 관련되는지, 전 세계 338개 계약의 기술통계·회귀분석과 질적 인터뷰를 통해 분석했다. 사회적 지향 투자자는 재무적·이중 목적 투자자보다 일관되게 더 큰 금액을 약정했으며, 인터뷰에서는 평판 위험, 현지 여건에 대한 제한적 이해, 성과 측정의 복잡성이 억제 요인으로 나타났다.
items.title: Investor Orientation and Commitment in Outcomes‐Based Public Service Contracts

items.abstract: Abstract Democratic backsliding continues to pose a clear danger to contemporary democracies. While a growing literature shows that voters often tolerate antidemocratic candidates when partisan or ideological incentives pull in that direction, we know less about whether support for democracy, institutional trust, political tolerance, and other democratic orientations ameliorate such temptations. We address this question with a systematic comparison of six measures of political culture as predictors of electoral resistance to antidemocratic candidates. Using candidate-choice conjoint experiments fielded in three democracies facing backsliding pressures—the United States, Poland, and South Korea—we find that several democratic orientations are associated with greater resistance to antidemocratic candidates. Among them, support for the core institutions and processes of liberal democracy stands out as the most consistent predictor. Its relationship with prodemocratic choice remains meaningful even in “cross-pressured” choices where partisan or ideological incentives pull voters away from the prodemocratic option. These findings suggest that political culture matters for democratic resilience, though some components of it matter much more consistently than others.

Christopher Claassen: Professor of Political Behaviour, School of Social and Political Sciences, University of Glasgow , Glasgow,

items.summary_ko: 정치문화가 민주주의 후퇴를 초래하는 반민주적 후보에 대한 유권자의 선거 저항을 완화하는지, 미국·폴란드·한국에서 후보 선택 컨조인트 실험으로 비교 분석했다. 자유민주주의의 핵심 제도와 절차에 대한 지지가 정당·이념적 유인이 상충하는 선택에서도 반민주적 후보에 대한 저항을 가장 일관되게 예측했으며, 다른 민주적 지향의 효과는 상대적으로 덜 일관됐다.
items.title: Voting for Democracy? Testing Political-Cultural Constraints on Democratic Backsliding

items.abstract: This study investigates sickness absenteeism and sickness presenteeism in the context of organizational development (OD) changes in the police force, focusing on health-related and motivational pathways. Using panel data from 407 employees from 36 Danish police units (1,021 observations), we analyze attendance patterns before the change, immediately after, and 1 year later. Findings reveal that sickness absenteeism is primarily influenced by the type of OD change rather than by job satisfaction or stress, while sickness presenteeism decreases with higher job satisfaction independent of the change type. Notably, employees experiencing an OD change aimed at supporting a long-term vision exhibit reduced sickness absence in the change period. OD changes focused on distributed leadership and enhancing employee motivation did not have the same effect on sickness absenteeism. These results underscore the importance of considering both motivational and health-related dynamics, as well as the type of change, in understanding attendance during OD change.
items.summary_ko: 덴마크 경찰 조직개발 변화 전후의 패널 자료를 활용해 스트레스와 직무만족도가 질병 결근 및 질병 출근에 미치는 경로와 변화 유형별 출근 양상을 분석했다. 질병 결근은 직무만족도나 스트레스보다 변화 유형의 영향을 주로 받았고, 장기 비전 지원형 변화에서는 결근이 감소했으며, 질병 출근은 변화 유형과 무관하게 직무만족도가 높을수록 감소했다.
items.title: Absenteeism and Presenteeism in Times of Change: The Role of Stress and Job Satisfaction

items.abstract: Collaborative platforms are increasingly used to coordinate digital public services across organizational boundaries, yet how they function in practice remains poorly understood. This study examines the coordination challenges such platforms face, drawing on Norway’s “life event” initiatives—programs designed to deliver integrated, user-centered digital services across government sectors. Based on document analysis and semi-structured interviews with 22 government actors and platform coordinators, the study finds that while collaborative platforms are designed to enable cross-sectoral interaction and co-creation, their effectiveness is constrained by structural barriers—including limited resources, unclear roles, and unsupportive regulatory frameworks—and by cultural tensions over norms, expectations, and interpretations of responsibility. These findings clarify the concept of collaborative platforms in public management research, showing how coordination challenges shape their operation and outcomes. The study contributes to digital governance scholarship by identifying the difficulties public managers face in steering and sustaining scalable collaborative arrangements for digital transformation and public service delivery.

Barbara Zyzak: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

items.summary_ko: 노르웨이의 ‘생애사건’ 디지털 서비스 նախաձեռն উদ্যোগ을 대상으로, 문서 분석과 정부 관계자·플랫폼 조정자 22명에 대한 반구조화 인터뷰를 통해 협업 플랫폼의 조정 과제를 분석했다. 협업 플랫폼은 부문 간 상호작용과 공동창출을 지원하도록 설계되지만, 제한된 자원·불명확한 역할·비지원적 규제라는 구조적 장벽과 규범·기대·책임 해석을 둘러싼 문화적 긴장으로 그 효과와 지속·확장 가능성이 제약되는 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: Collaborative platforms in digital government: structural and cultural barriers to coordination

items.abstract: Although public healthcare workers frequently encounter negative interactions with patients and care recipients, research on how such contact shapes staff behavior is limited. The purpose of the current study is to advance knowledge of _how_ and _under what conditions_ negative beneficiary contact is related to service-oriented organizational citizenship behaviors (OCBs) in public healthcare organizations. Drawing on the relational job design perspective, this study examines prosocial impact as a mediator of the link between negative beneficiary contact and service-oriented OCBs, and the buffering role of service-oriented high-performance work systems (HPWS) on this mediated relationship. Two time-lagged, multisource datasets from nurses and their direct supervisors in hospitals in Romania (Study 1) and Egypt (Study 2) were used to test the proposed model. The results showed that prosocial impact mediates the relationship between negative beneficiary contact and service OCBs, but this indirect link was insignificant when perceptions of HPWS were high. Implications for public management theory and practice are discussed.

Ahmed Mohammed Sayed Mostafa: Leeds University Business School, University of Leeds

items.summary_ko: 공공의료 종사자의 부정적 수혜자 접촉이 서비스 지향 조직시민행동과 어떤 관계를 맺는지, 그리고 서비스 지향 고성과작업시스템(HPWS)이 이를 어떻게 조절하는지 검토했다. 루마니아와 이집트 병원의 간호사·직속 상사를 대상으로 한 시차·다원 자료 분석 결과, 친사회적 영향이 두 변수의 관계를 매개했지만 HPWS 인식이 높을 때 이 간접효과는 유의하지 않았다.
items.title: How and When Does Negative Beneficiary Contact Relate to Service Behaviors? Unpacking the Roles of Prosocial Impact and Service-Oriented High-Performance Work Systems in Public Healthcare

items.abstract: Why do seemingly minor acts of citizen disrespect matter for police retention? Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and sociometer theory, this study examines how citizen incivility shapes officers’ withdrawal processes over time. Using a three-wave longitudinal survey of 1,397 police officers, we test whether baseline exposure to citizen incivility predicts subsequent trajectories of work disengagement and turnover intention. We argue that citizen incivility functions as a low intensity but psychologically consequential interpersonal cue that subtly threatens officers’ perceived social standing, depleting psychological resources, fostering disengagement, and ultimately increasing turnover intention. We further propose that perceived organizational support (POS), as a valued resource and a signal of institutional recognition, buffers these adverse effects. Results confirm that citizen incivility indirectly predicts turnover intention through disengagement, and that POS attenuates this pathway. These findings advance understanding of resource-loss dynamics in public service contexts and highlight the protective role of organizational support in sustaining frontline engagement and retention.

Cathy Y. Guo: IESEG School of Management, Univ. Lille, CNRS, UMR 9221 - LEM - Lille Économie Management
Martin Storme: IESEG School of Management, Univ. Lille, CNRS, UMR 9221 - LEM - Lille Économie Management

items.summary_ko: 시민의 무례가 경찰관의 업무 이탈과 이직 의향에 미치는 종단적 영향을 검토하고, 조직지원인식이 이를 완화하는지 1,397명을 대상으로 한 3시점 설문으로 분석했다. 시민의 무례는 업무 이탈을 매개로 이직 의향을 높였으며, 조직지원인식은 이 경로를 약화시켰다.
items.title: When police officers surrender: the effect of citizen incivility on withdrawal and turnover

items.abstract: Abstract Perceptions of social norms, and how those norms change over time, play a central role in shaping how people understand and respond to political divides. We developed and iteratively refined dynamic‐norm messages about bipartisan attitude change to reduce divisive outparty perceptions and attitudes in a US context. We first identified real‐world issues that gained support over time among both Democrats and Republicans and were judged as believable. Study 1 documented systematic misperceptions of attitude change across a range of social issues and linked these misperceptions to colder outparty feelings. We then tested intervention messages that adapted standard static‐norm templates with the addition of information about change over time (dynamic norm; Study 2). This intervention increased expectations of future common ground but did not reliably improve downstream outparty attitudes. Next, we tested a refined intervention message that isolated dynamic norm information (Study 3). The refined dynamic norm message increased expected common ground and expected future feelings of belonging among the outparty and was associated with small but reliable increases in outparty warmth and positive outparty impressions relative to control. These results suggest that emphasizing trajectories of public opinion without highlighting current partisan gaps may be a useful strategy for reducing polarization.

Ashley Fabrizio: More in Common New York New York USA
Jordan Wylie: Department of Psychology Cornell University Ithaca New York USA
Liane Young: Department of Psychology and Neuroscience Boston College Chestnut Hill Massachusetts USA
Stylianos Syropoulos: College of Global Futures, Arizona State University Tempe Arizona USA
Trystan Loustau: Department of Psychology and Neuroscience Boston College Chestnut Hill Massachusetts USA

items.summary_ko: 미국 맥락에서 정당 간 태도 변화에 대한 동적 규범 인식의 오류와 이를 교정하는 메시지가 상대 정당에 대한 인식과 감정에 미치는 영향을 설문 연구와 개입 실험으로 검토했다. 사람들은 다양한 사회 이슈에서 양당의 공통 지지가 증가한 정도를 체계적으로 오인했으며, 현재의 정당 간 격차를 강조하지 않고 태도 변화의 추세만 제시한 메시지는 공통 기반과 소속감에 대한 기대를 높이고 상대 정당에 대한 호감과 긍정적 인상을 소폭 증가시켰다.
items.title: Partisans misperceive and are influenced by dynamic norms

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Public service motivation (PSM) is widely recognized as a predictor of positive outcomes, yet relatively little is known about how it can be deliberately cultivated. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, the present research investigates whether and how exposure to moral exemplars embedded in public‐sector training enhances PSM. Employing a multi‐method design that combines a recall experiment with a field survey, we find that exposure to uncommon moral exemplars elicits moral elevation, which functions as a replenishment of psychological resources and, in turn, strengthens public employees' PSM. Moreover, this mediating mechanism is moderated by cognitive load, such that public employees experiencing greater cognitive demands derive stronger motivational benefits from moral elevation. By identifying moral elevation as a psychological resource mechanism and cognitive load as a boundary condition, this research opens the “black box” of PSM development. It highlights how training can serve as an institutional platform for delivering specific moral content that cultivates and sustains public employees' motivation to serve.

Bangcheng Liu: Shanghai Jiao Tong University Shanghai China
Xiaoyu Wang: East China Normal University Shanghai China
Yuming Wang: National University of Singapore Singapore Singapore

items.summary_ko: 공공부문 교육에서 도덕적 모범 인물에 노출되는 것이 공공서비스동기(PSM)를 어떻게 강화하는지, 회상 실험과 현장 설문을 결합해 분석했다. 드문 도덕적 모범 인물에 대한 노출은 도덕적 고양을 유발하고, 이것이 심리적 자원 보충을 통해 PSM을 높였으며, 인지적 부담이 클수록 그 동기 효과가 강했다.
items.title: Inspired to Serve: Exposure to Moral Models to Enhance Public Service Motivation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The early city management profession experienced appalling rates of attrition. This problem of “professional mortality” had been clearly recognized by the end of World War I: causes of attrition included threats and violence against managers, intense political interference in managers' work, and interpersonal missteps. Yet the organized management profession and advocates of the manager plan actively ignored threats and were unwilling to respond collectively or officially to political interference; leading scholars recognized but did not publicly discuss common interpersonal problems faced by managers. This silence on the underlying causes of turnover marked an effort to protect the manager plan's viability in the face of growing electoral opposition during the 1920s, placing the interests of the profession above its practicing members. The optimistic, rationalist discourses of advocates, scholars, and professional leaders rested on self‐conscious denial of uncomfortable realities; a full historical accounting may help avoid repeating these mistakes.

Ben Merriman: School of Public Affairs & Administration University of Kansas Lawrence Kansas USA

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 초기 도시관리 전문직에서 높은 이직률인 ‘전문직 사망’의 원인과 이를 둘러싼 조직적 침묵을 분석한다. 역사적 자료에 따르면 폭력과 위협, 정치적 개입, 대인관계상의 실수가 이직을 초래했지만, 전문직 조직과 옹호자들은 1920년대 선거 반대에 대응해 도시관리자제도의 생존을 우선하며 이러한 문제를 공개적으로 인정하거나 집단적으로 대응하지 않았다.
items.title: The “Professional Mortality” Problem in Early City Management: A Study of Organized Denial

items.abstract: Previous research on performance gaming behavior has primarily focused on data manipulation and effort manipulation. This article examines strategic reporting, a broad form of performance gaming in public organizations, by identifying four strategies: text-only reporting, social comparison benchmark shifting, historical comparison benchmark shifting, and absolute level absence. Drawing on theories of bounded rationality and blame avoidance, it investigates how positive and negative performance feedback shape strategic reporting behavior. Using data from Chinese municipal governments (2013–2019), logit model results suggest systematic variation across four strategic reporting strategies. All four strategies are positively associated with negative performance feedback, while all strategies but historical benchmark shifting are negatively associated with positive performance feedback. These findings contribute to the literature on performance gaming and performance feedback, while offering practical implications for strengthening governmental transparency and accountability.
items.summary_ko: 중국 지방정부의 정부업무보고(2013~2019년) 자료를 활용해, 제한된 합리성과 책임회피 이론에 기반하여 긍정·부정 성과 피드백이 네 가지 전략적 보고 방식에 미치는 영향을 로짓모형으로 분석했다. 네 가지 전략 모두 부정적 성과 피드백과 정(+)의 관련성을 보였으며, 역사적 비교 기준 이동을 제외한 세 전략은 긍정적 성과 피드백과 부(-)의 관련성을 보였다.
items.title: Performance Feedback and Strategic Reporting—Evidence from China’s Government Work Report

items.abstract: When governments mandate collaboration, data often becomes the currency for coordination and control. This study examines how data infrastructures shape collaboration and power dynamics within US homelessness service networks, where Continuums of Care (CoCs) coordinate providers through the mandated Homeless Management Information System (HMIS). This study analyzes data from 12 semi-structured interviews of CoC leaders and service providers in Central Florida using thematic analysis informed by the data value chain framework. The findings show that data sharing can enhance coordination and accountability but also reinforce power asymmetries between mandators and collaborators. While standardized data enable collaboration among providers, disparities in resources, analytical capacity, and decision authority constrain equitable participation. The study extends the data value chain model and shows that data-driven collaboration in mandated networks can promote collective learning while also enforcing compliance. These findings suggest that investments in analytical capacity and shared governance can strengthen collaboration in mandated networks.
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 미국 노숙인 서비스 네트워크에서 의무화된 노숙인정보관리시스템(HMIS)의 데이터 인프라가 제공기관 간 협력과 권력관계에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지, 중앙플로리다 CoC 지도자와 서비스 제공자 12명의 반구조화 인터뷰를 주제분석해 검토했다. 표준화된 데이터는 조정·책무성과 집단학습을 높일 수 있지만, 자원·분석역량·의사결정 권한의 격차로 참여의 형평성이 제약되고 데이터 공유가 순응을 강제하는 권력 비대칭을 강화할 수 있는 것으로 나타났다.
items.title: Data-Driven Collaboration in Mandated Networks: US Homelessness Services

items.abstract: How does context influence the practice of public values assessment (PVA)? This study examines how PVA is shaped in practice within a Dutch government organization. It constitutes a qualitative case study at the Dutch Central Government Real Estate Agency, based on interviews with policymakers and public managers, complemented by literature review and validation sessions within the agency. The study identifies four contextual tensions that shape how PVA is performed: (1) single-actor, single-level activity versus multi-actor, multi-level activity; (2) role clarity versus role ambiguity; (3) individual discretion versus organizational steering; and (4) emergent activity versus deliberate activity. The findings show that PVA is not a standalone analytical exercise, but a situated and ongoing practice shaped by organizational roles, governance arrangements, and interactions between actors. By grounding these tensions empirically, this study advances public value theory by showing how context conditions the practice of PVA in real-world settings.
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 네덜란드 정부기관에서 맥락이 공공가치 평가(PVA)의 실제 수행에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 질적 사례연구로 분석했다. 인터뷰와 문헌 검토, 기관 내 검증 세션을 통해 PVA가 독립적 분석이 아니라 행위자의 역할, 거버넌스 arrangements, 상호작용에 의해 형성되는 지속적 실천이며, 네 가지 맥락적 긴장이 이를 좌우한다는 점을 밝혔다.
items.title: How context and tensions shape public values assessment: findings from a case study of a Dutch agency

items.abstract: This study examines how gender equity in educational achievement relates to the satisfaction of three key stakeholders: students, parents, and teachers. Using cross-national panel data from the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS), covering 56 countries from 2011 to 2019, we link gender gaps in student math and science performance to student and parent satisfaction with schooling, as well as teacher satisfaction with their jobs. We find that gender inequity is associated with lower satisfaction, but parents with a female student and higher SES respond to the gender inequity the most. These findings extend the citizen satisfaction and public service equity literatures by showing that different stakeholders in the same public service system can respond quite differently to inequities, with implications for how governments communicate about and address performance gaps and equity concerns.
items.summary_ko: 56개국 TIMSS 2011~2019 국가 간 패널 자료를 활용해 교육 성취도의 성별 격차와 학생·학부모의 학교 만족도 및 교사의 직무 만족도 간 관계를 분석했다. 성별 불평등은 낮은 만족도와 관련되며, 여학생 학부모와 사회경제적 지위가 높은 학부모가 성별 격차에 가장 크게 반응했다.
items.title: Public service equity and stakeholder satisfaction: evidence from 56 countries on how parents, teachers, and students respond to gender gaps in education

items.abstract: How does context influence the practice of public values assessment (PVA)? This study examines how PVA is shaped in practice within a Dutch government organization. It constitutes a qualitative case study at the Dutch Central Government Real Estate Agency, based on interviews with policymakers and public managers, complemented by literature review and validation sessions within the agency. The study identifies four contextual tensions that shape how PVA is performed: (1) single-actor, single-level activity versus multi-actor, multi-level activity; (2) role clarity versus role ambiguity; (3) individual discretion versus organizational steering; and (4) emergent activity versus deliberate activity. The findings show that PVA is not a standalone analytical exercise, but a situated and ongoing practice shaped by organizational roles, governance arrangements, and interactions between actors. By grounding these tensions empirically, this study advances public value theory by showing how context conditions the practice of PVA in real-world settings.
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 네덜란드 정부기관에서 맥락이 공공가치 평가(PVA)의 실제 수행에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 질적 사례연구로 분석했다. 인터뷰와 문헌 검토, 기관 내 검증 세션을 통해 PVA가 독립적 분석이 아니라 행위자의 역할, 거버넌스 arrangements, 상호작용에 의해 형성되는 지속적 실천이며, 네 가지 맥락적 긴장이 이를 좌우한다는 점을 밝혔다.
items.title: How context and tensions shape public values assessment: findings from a case study of a Dutch agency

items.abstract: This study examines how gender equity in educational achievement relates to the satisfaction of three key stakeholders: students, parents, and teachers. Using cross-national panel data from the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS), covering 56 countries from 2011 to 2019, we link gender gaps in student math and science performance to student and parent satisfaction with schooling, as well as teacher satisfaction with their jobs. We find that gender inequity is associated with lower satisfaction, but parents with a female student and higher SES respond to the gender inequity the most. These findings extend the citizen satisfaction and public service equity literatures by showing that different stakeholders in the same public service system can respond quite differently to inequities, with implications for how governments communicate about and address performance gaps and equity concerns.
items.summary_ko: 56개국 TIMSS 2011~2019 국가 간 패널 자료를 활용해 교육 성취도의 성별 격차와 학생·학부모의 학교 만족도 및 교사의 직무 만족도 간 관계를 분석했다. 성별 불평등은 낮은 만족도와 관련되며, 여학생 학부모와 사회경제적 지위가 높은 학부모가 성별 격차에 가장 크게 반응했다.
items.title: Public service equity and stakeholder satisfaction: evidence from 56 countries on how parents, teachers, and students respond to gender gaps in education
